title: ‘Why is she wearing shorts’: How family outing at Pune fort turned into assault

Authorities have launched a search to apprehend the eight accused individuals.

title: Bulldozers roll outside Pakistan High Commission in Delhi; barricades removed
content: Indian authorities removed the external security cordon around the Pakistan High Commission. Traffic bollards and barricades were dismantled from the diplomatic compound premises. This action effectively eliminated the external security perimeter outside the high commission. The Pakistan High Commission is situated within the Chanakyapuri diplomatic enclave.

title: No 2800 km dash this time: Qamran Iqbal arrives early, ready for Duleep Trophy challenge
content: Called up less than 24 hours before the Ranji Trophy final, Qamran Iqbal travelled nearly 2,800 km from Srinagar to Hubballi before scoring an unbeaten 160 that helped Jammu and Kashmir win their maiden title. The 24-year-old reflects on the whirlwind journey, J&K's rise and his ambition to shine in the Duleep Trophy. North Zone will take on West Zone at the BCCI’s Centre of Excellence (CoE) from Sunday.

title: In dry Gujarat, spurious booze kills 6 at party thrown by cop; 25 in hospital
content: Six people died and twenty-five were hospitalized after drinking methanol-spiked liquor.  The incident occurred in Bhavnagar district, with victims consuming liquor from Royal Stag bottles.  Questions arose regarding alleged police reporting delays, prompting an investigation by the State Monitoring Cell.  Patients reported breathlessness and vision loss, with officials warning of kidney complications.  The liquor was manufactured and sold locally in Bhavnagar, and suspects have been detained.

title: OpenAI CFO to employees: Don’t worry about Anthropic going public
content: The CFO of OpenAI recently announced that a public offering is anticipated by 2027, emphasizing that this IPO represents a significant fundraising achievement rather than a final destination. She responded to worries regarding competitor Anthropic, which may go public sooner. OpenAI has shown impressive revenue growth and user engagement, though recent departures of key executives have raised questions about the company's stability.

title: Tarun Tejpal moves SC against Bombay HC conviction, 10-year jail term
content: Tarun Tejpal has appealed the Bombay high court's conviction and ten-year sentence.  The high court overturned his earlier acquittal in a 2013 sexual assault case.  He was convicted of raping a junior colleague in a Goa hotel elevator.  The Goa government also seeks a life sentence, deeming the current punishment lenient.  Tejpal previously claimed political targeting in the ongoing legal proceedings.

title: ‘Manan, it’s done bro’: Dipke calls ‘legal cockroaches’ to protest against BCI chief
content: A protest is planned against the Bar Council of India chairman.  This demonstration follows a withdrawn directive concerning NALSAR University of Law students.  The All India Young Advocates Association is organizing the demonstration.  The BCI chairman had previously apologized to law students for his words.  The protest seeks accountability and the chairman's resignation from his position.

title: 'Don't daydream about my jawani': Kangana Ranaut to Baba Ramdev
content: Kangana Ranaut criticized Baba Ramdev's comments on her remarks about young protesters.  She told the yoga guru not to speculate about her personal life.  Ramdev had questioned Ranaut's past deeds and youth in a media interaction.  Ranaut referenced a Supreme Court case involving Patanjali's misleading advertisements.  Both figures engaged in a public dispute following Ranaut's controversial statements.

title: Microsoft AI CMO Andra Mallard leaves after just 6 months
content: Microsoft AI's chief marketing officer, Andra Mallard, is leaving the company soon. She plans to relocate her family to Europe for personal reasons next August. Mallard's departure coincides with a strategic marketing shift within Microsoft's AI division. The company is consolidating its Copilot apps into a single unified application. This move follows broader changes within the Microsoft AI unit.

title: In the 1970s, man bought part of Washington island; now he's its only resident
content: Protection Island in Washington was once planned as a holiday community with 800 homes. Marty Bluewater bought a piece of the island in the 1970s, but conservationists later fought to protect its important wildlife habitat. In 1982, the entire 400-acre island became a National Wildlife Refuge. Bluewater was allowed to stay and eventually became its only human resident.

title: 29 copper spheres found beneath Amethi house site; ASI team examines them
content: During construction work in Bhanauli village, workers discovered twenty-nine large metal spheres buried deep within the ground. These intriguing copper spheres, each measuring sixty centimeters across, resembled ancient munitions. Local police and the Uttar Pradesh Archaeology Department quickly secured the unusual find. Specialists are now engaged in examining the spheres to determine their historical significance and origin, with plans for additional archaeological research to ascertain their context.

title: Ex-Meta employee claims it had a ‘don’t ask, don’t tell’ policy on child safety issues
content: A former Meta safety researcher testified against the company in court. Arturo Béjar claimed Meta ignored child safety concerns to protect its business. He stated the company had a "don't ask, don't tell" policy regarding underage users. Béjar also criticized CEO Mark Zuckerberg for insufficient action on safety issues. This testimony is part of a major trial brought by 29 US states.

title: Andhra woman dies in freak accident after elevator moves with door open
content: A woman died in a horrifying lift accident in Ongole on Sunday. The elevator at Surya Towers allegedly moved down suddenly with its door open. The victim, Vanitha, was caught off guard and suffered severe injuries. She was rushed to the hospital but succumbed to her injuries later. A video of the incident has gone viral on social media.

title: ABVP, Left-leaning student groups clash on Jadavpur University campus

Several students sustained injuries during the confrontation, with some requiring hospital treatment. The confrontation reportedly began over a student union meeting and continued late into the night. Both groups accused each other of bringing outsiders onto the university campus. Protests have been announced by both student organizations following the incident.

title: 4 killed, 7 injured in accident inside Hanogi tunnel in Himachal

title: 'You must blame your father, sisters, brothers… but ... ': Quote of the day by Katharine Hepburn

She believed that individuals have the capacity to shift their viewpoints and navigate challenges effectively. Hepburn’s illustrious career serves as a testament to her philosophy, as she faced and conquered numerous obstacles in Hollywood. Her journey was underscored by resilience and a fierce dedication to her craft, establishing an enduring legacy through her distinctive acting style.

title: India recreate Ganguly's shirt-waving celebration after beating England at Lord's

title: Amit Shah chairs Southern Zonal Council meeting in Tamil Nadu

This council acts as a vital forum for fostering dialogue between state governments and the Centre, demonstrating a commitment to cooperative federalism and effective dispute resolution.

title: ‘Must not be used to legitimise terrorists’: India seeks transparency in UNSC

title: Travis Kelce's $531K salary to $90 million net worth: His money journey

content: out of 72 private homeopathy medical colleges in Maharashtra, at least 34 (47%) are established by trusts or societies that have political connections cutting across party lines . these colleges with strong political connections account for almost 3,000 seats, or about half of the total homeopathy seats in the state .

title: Police cannot investigate sex determination offences under PCPNDT Act: SC
content: the supreme court ruled that police cannot ordinarily investigate offences related to foetal sex determination under the PCPNDT Act . a bench said the police can have only a limited and supplementary role when required by the Appropriate Authority (AA) the court upheld the view taken by the Allahabad .

title: Former Congress MP Sajjan Kumar, convicted in 1984 anti-Sikh riots case, dies at 80
content:
Sajjan Kumar (File photo)

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Sajjan Kumar, convicted in cases related to the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, died at the age of 80 on Thursday. He breathed his last at Delhi's Safdarjung Hospital. The anti-Sikh riots followed the October 31, 1984, assassination of then-Prime Minister and Congress leader Indira Gandhi by her Sikh bodyguards in retaliation for the Army's Operation Blue Star in June that year.(Developing story)

title: Russia unleashes ballistic, cruise, hypersonic missiles and drones on Ukraine
content: 168 drones and ballistic missiles were fired in a large overnight air assault . the barrage damaged residential and public buildings, sparked fires and disrupted power supplies . a fire tore through a nine-storey residential building, destroying its upper floors and killing seven people .

title: NALSAR row sparks fresh protest: Lawyers demand resignation of BCI chief Manan Mishra
content: lawyers protest outside the bar Council of India office demanding resignation of chairman Manan Kumar Mishra . the protest came days after the council’s now-withdrawn order targeting the enrolment of NALSAR University’s graduating batch drew criticism from sections of the legal fraternity .

title: Gandhi manuscript fetches Rs 16.2 crore at Saffronart, sets world auction record
content: a thought for the day isn’t just a WhatsApp forward; it can be worth a fortune if it’s written in Bapu’s hand . on Wednesday, Mahatma Gandhi’s ‘A Thought of the Day’ sold for Rs 16.2 crore ($1.7 million) at a Saffronart auction .
